q: What is needed where a tubing (thin-wall) trap connects to the drain?
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 10
n: Tubing traps have thinner walls than pipe, so an adapter makes the transition to the drain fitting.

q: May food waste from a disposer be discharged into a grease interceptor?
o: Yes, if the interceptor is doubled in size
Yes, if a strainer is fitted
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 10
n: Ground food fills the interceptor with solids and stops it separating grease.

q: What is the maximum distance from the trap weir to the vent for a 76 mm trap arm?
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 10
n: Trap arm limits: 32 mm 0.76 m, 38 mm 1.07 m, 51 mm 1.52 m, 76 mm 1.83 m, 102 mm and up 3.05 m. Past these, the trap seal can be siphoned before air reaches it from the vent.

q: Is a grease trap required for a private house kitchen?
o: Yes, if the house has more than one kitchen
Only if the house has a septic tank
No, not for individual private living quarters
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 10
n: Grease traps are required for restaurants and other food service, not for single dwellings.

q: What must be marked on a tubing trap?
o: The tubing gauge and the maker's name or mark
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 10
n: Marking lets the inspector check that the trap is thick enough and is an approved product.

q: Is an S-trap allowed under the plumbing code?
o: Yes, if it has a cleanout
Yes, on the ground floor only
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 10
n: An S-trap sends water straight down after the seal, so the full-pipe flow siphons the seal out. Prohibited trap types are the S-trap, bell trap, crown-vented trap, and traps that depend on moving parts or hidden partitions.

q: What is required on a floor drain that could receive reverse flow from the sewer?
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 10
n: A backwater valve closes when sewage backs up, so it cannot flood out of the floor drain.

q: Which fixture has an integral (built-in) trap?
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 10
n: The water closet bowl holds its own seal, so no separate trap is fitted.

q: Is a double trap (two traps in series on one fixture) allowed?
o: Yes, if both traps are vented
Yes, if one trap is a drum trap
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 10
n: Air trapped between two seals stops the water from flowing and can blow out a seal.

q: May a clothes washer or laundry tub drain into a kitchen-sink trap?
o: Yes, if the sink is within 1.5 m
No, it needs its own trap
Yes, if a disposer is fitted
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 10
n: A washer's large, sudden discharge would back up into the kitchen sink.

q: How many approved slip-joint fittings may be used on the outlet side of a trap?
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 10
n: Slip joints can loosen and leak sewer gas, so their number downstream of the seal is limited.

q: Except for water closets and urinals, where must a fixture vent NOT connect to the trap arm?
o: Above the weir of the trap
On the vertical, at or above the trap outlet
Below the weir of the trap
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 10
n: A vent below the weir acts as a drain, fills with waste and siphons the trap. It must take off at or above the weir.

q: Under what condition may a drum trap be installed?
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 10
n: A drum trap holds a large volume of water. It must still be vented like any other trap.

q: What size of object must a laundry-tub strainer (basket) stop?
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 10
n: The basket catches lint, buttons and other items before they reach the trap.

q: How much fixture flow may be connected to a grease trap?
o: No more than its certified flow rate
No more than 5 times its certified flow rate
No more than 2.5 times its certified flow rate in L/min
Any amount, if it is cleaned often
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 10
n: Not all fixtures drain at once, so the connected flow may exceed the rating, but only up to 2.5 times.

q: What type of trap is used for a shower or floor drain?
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 10
n: The P-trap is the standard approved trap. Prohibited trap types are the S-trap, bell trap, crown-vented trap, and traps that depend on moving parts or hidden partitions.

q: What must a fixture discharging into a grease trap have?
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 10
n: The flow control keeps water moving through slowly enough for grease to separate.

q: What minimum water seal must an industrial interceptor have?
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 10
n: Interceptors hold oily or gritty waste, so a deeper seal is needed than the 51–102 mm of a fixture trap.

q: What depth of water seal must a fixture trap have?
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 10
n: Less than 51 mm evaporates or siphons too easily. More than 102 mm holds back solids and fouls.

q: How deep must a sand interceptor be below its outlet invert?
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 10
n: The deep sump below the outlet gives sand room to settle.

q: What slope must a trap arm have?
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 10
n: The trap arm must fall so that it does not hold water, but not so steeply that its outlet falls below the trap weir.

q: A grease trap serves 2 fixtures. What flow rate and grease retention capacity does it need?
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 10
n: Grease trap sizing: 1 fixture 76 L/min and 18 kg grease; 2 fixtures 95 L/min and 23 kg; 3 fixtures 132 L/min and 32 kg; 4 fixtures 189 L/min and 45 kg.

q: What minimum area must a sand interceptor have?
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 10
n: Enough surface area slows the water so sand and grit settle out.

q: Where must the location of interceptors be shown?
o: Only on a tag on the interceptor
Nowhere; the plumber decides on site
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 10
n: Interceptors need regular cleaning, so their location must be recorded on the plans.

q: What is the maximum distance from a water-closet flange to its vent?
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 10
n: A closet is a 76 mm trap arm, so its vent must be within 1.83 m.

q: Where must an automobile wash rack drain?
o: Straight into the storm drain in the street
Through an oil interceptor, kept free of rain
Straight into the sanitary sewer, untreated
Into a seepage pit dug beside the rack
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 10
n: Car wash water carries oil, grease and grit. Rain must be kept out so it does not overload the interceptor.

q: A grease trap serves 3 fixtures. What flow rate and grease retention capacity does it need?
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 10
n: Grease trap sizing: 1 fixture 76 L/min and 18 kg grease; 2 fixtures 95 L/min and 23 kg; 3 fixtures 132 L/min and 32 kg; 4 fixtures 189 L/min and 45 kg.

q: A grease trap serves 1 fixture. What flow rate and grease retention capacity does it need?
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 10
n: Grease trap sizing: 1 fixture 76 L/min and 18 kg grease; 2 fixtures 95 L/min and 23 kg; 3 fixtures 132 L/min and 32 kg; 4 fixtures 189 L/min and 45 kg.

q: What is the minimum length of a trap arm?
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 10
n: A trap arm that is too short lets the vent opening sit too close to the trap outlet.

q: Up to three laundry tubs share one trap. How far apart at most may they be?
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 10
n: They must also be single-compartment tubs set at the same level.

q: What is the maximum distance from the trap weir to the vent for a 32 mm trap arm?
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 10
n: Trap arm limits: 32 mm 0.76 m, 38 mm 1.07 m, 51 mm 1.52 m, 76 mm 1.83 m, 102 mm and up 3.05 m. Past these, the trap seal can be siphoned before air reaches it from the vent.

q: How many single-compartment laundry tubs may share one trap?
o: Only one, with its own trap and vent
Up to six, if the trap is 76 mm
Any number, as long as each is vented
Up to three, set level and close together
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 10
n: Adjacent compartments of the same kind can share a trap when their outlets are close and level.

q: Is a bell trap or crown-vented trap allowed?
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 10
n: Prohibited trap types are the S-trap, bell trap, crown-vented trap, and traps that depend on moving parts or hidden partitions.

q: What is the minimum pipe size for a sand interceptor outlet?
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 10
n: Sand interceptors serve floors that are hosed down, so they need a large outlet.

q: What is the maximum distance from the trap weir to the vent for a 102 mm or larger trap arm?
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 10
n: Trap arm limits: 32 mm 0.76 m, 38 mm 1.07 m, 51 mm 1.52 m, 76 mm 1.83 m, 102 mm and up 3.05 m. Past these, the trap seal can be siphoned before air reaches it from the vent.

q: In an interceptor, how large must the outlet section be?
o: At least 25% of the inlet section area
At least equal to the inlet section
At least twice the inlet section
At least 50% of the inlet section area
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 10
n: The outlet section still needs enough volume to hold back what the inlet section did not catch.

q: What minimum wall thickness must tubing traps have?
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 10
n: Thin-wall brass traps must be heavy enough not to corrode through. Urinal traps are excluded.

q: How many traps may a single trap arm serve?
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 10
n: Each trap has its own arm to its vent. Otherwise one fixture's flow could siphon another's seal.

q: A grease trap serves 4 fixtures. What flow rate and grease retention capacity does it need?
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 10
n: Grease trap sizing: 1 fixture 76 L/min and 18 kg grease; 2 fixtures 95 L/min and 23 kg; 3 fixtures 132 L/min and 32 kg; 4 fixtures 189 L/min and 45 kg.

q: In a commercial kitchen, how is a food-waste disposer connected?
o: Straight to the building drain without a trap
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 10
n: Disposers must not discharge through grease interceptors, and each needs its own trap.

q: What is the maximum length of a fixture tailpiece?
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 10
n: A long tailpiece gathers speed and can siphon the trap seal.

q: What type of trap is used under a lavatory?
o: A drum trap without a vent
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 10
n: The P-trap turns horizontal after the seal, which keeps the seal from being siphoned.

q: What is the maximum distance from the trap weir to the vent for a 51 mm trap arm?
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 10
n: Trap arm limits: 32 mm 0.76 m, 38 mm 1.07 m, 51 mm 1.52 m, 76 mm 1.83 m, 102 mm and up 3.05 m. Past these, the trap seal can be siphoned before air reaches it from the vent.

q: What must the inside of a trap be like?
o: Fitted with a baffle to trap solids
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 10
n: Smooth waterways let the trap clean itself with each flush. Partitions and moving parts are banned.

q: What is the maximum distance from the trap weir to the vent for a 38 mm trap arm?
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 10
n: Trap arm limits: 32 mm 0.76 m, 38 mm 1.07 m, 51 mm 1.52 m, 76 mm 1.83 m, 102 mm and up 3.05 m. Past these, the trap seal can be siphoned before air reaches it from the vent.

q: What does a trap primer do?
o: Pumps out a trap when it is clogged
Keeps a floor drain trap topped up with water
Vents the trap to the roof through a valve
Opens the drain when the floor floods
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 10
n: Floor drains that rarely get water lose their seal by evaporation. A primer tops it up.

q: What must every floor drain have?
ref: 1999 Revised National Plumbing Code of the Philippines, Chapter 10
n: Every fixture connected to the drainage system needs a trap to keep sewer gas out.
